chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al- Attar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Do not consummate (the marriage with your) female slave until she reaches the age of nine or ten. He added, 'I either heard nine or ten.'
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum age for consummating marriage with a female slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Kisāl* highlights the foundational Shia juristic view on the minimum age for consummating marriage with a female slave, anchoring it in the era of the Imams. The variation between 'nine' and 'ten' years reflects the flexibility in early hadith transmission and underscores the distinction between biological puberty (bulugh) and legal capacity (rahim) in Shia fiqh. It serves as a primary textual basis for the majority opinion that nine lunar years constitutes the threshold of maturity for marriage purposes.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 9-15 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Safvan ibn Yahya, on the authority of Musa ibn Bakr, on the authority of Zurarah that Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) said,
“Do not consummate (the marriage with your) female slave until she reaches the age of nine or ten.” He added, “I either heard nine or ten.”
